title: A URL shortener
requirements: Anyone can turn a long link into a short one.
Opening a short link sends the browser to the long one, fast.
Short links keep working for years.
Far more people open links than create them.
checklist: Where is each short code stored, and how do two servers avoid making the same code?
Which path is the busy one (opening links), and what makes it fast?
What happens to opening links if the database is slow or down?
What stops one person creating millions of links?
If you add a cache, what goes in it, and when does an entry go stale?

title: A chat app
requirements: People send messages to each other and to groups.
Messages appear for the other person within a moment, while they're online.
Messages sent while someone is offline are there when they come back.
Every conversation stays in order, and no message is lost.
checklist: How does a server push a new message to a phone that's waiting?
Where is a message saved before you tell the sender it was sent?
How is the order of messages in one conversation decided?
What happens to a message for someone who is offline?
What happens when the server holding someone's connection crashes?

title: A news feed
requirements: People follow other people and see their recent posts, newest first.
Opening the feed is fast, even for someone who follows thousands.
A few accounts have millions of followers.
checklist: When someone posts, is it copied into followers' feeds at once, or gathered when a feed opens?
What does your choice cost when an account with millions of followers posts?
Where are finished feeds kept, and what happens if that store loses them?
Which work happens in the background, through a queue?

title: Taking payments
requirements: Shoppers pay for orders with a card, through an outside payment provider.
A shopper is never charged twice for one order, even when the network fails.
The shop always knows which orders are paid.
checklist: If a reply from the payment provider is lost, how does a retry avoid a second charge?
How does your system learn about a payment that finished after a timeout?
What happens when the same webhook event arrives twice?
Where is the record of each payment kept, and can it be changed afterwards?
What does the shopper see while a payment's result is still unknown?

title: An AI chat assistant
requirements: People chat with an assistant that calls a language model.
Replies start appearing quickly instead of all at once at the end.
Each conversation remembers what was said earlier.
The model provider limits how many requests the service may send.
checklist: Where is the conversation history kept, given the model doesn't remember between requests?
What happens when the provider's rate limit is reached?
What happens to a reply if the user's connection drops halfway?
Which actions, if any, can the assistant take, and who approves them?
How would you know a new version answers worse than the old one?

title: A notification system
requirements: Other services ask it to tell a user something, by push, email or SMS.
Each user's settings decide which channels they get, and quiet hours.
A slow email provider must not hold up push notifications.
checklist: Where are user settings checked, before or after a notification is queued?
Does each channel have its own queue? What happens if one backs up?
What happens to a notification whose provider keeps failing?
How do you avoid sending the same notification twice after a retry?
